chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Bukhtuj, so he said: 'If it is sweet and colors the vessel,' and its owner said: 'Two-thirds of it has gone away and one-third remains, so drink it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for drinking boiled grape juice (Bukhtuj) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of 'Al-Bukhtuj' (concentrated grape syrup) by linking its status to the degree of evaporation, specifically when two-thirds of the liquid has reduced. The Imam’s criterion—that the residue must be sweet enough to color the vessel—serves as a practical sensory test to ensure the juice is sufficiently concentrated and distinct from fresh grape juice, thereby avoiding confusion with wine. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly approach of using tangible physical indicators to determine the legal status of food and drink items in daily life.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about Al-Bukhtuj (boiled grape juice), so heasws said: ‘If its sweetness had coloured the vessel and its owner says that two-third of it has gone away (evaporated) and there remains the third, so drink it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Bakhtaj (boiled juice). He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is sweet with an indication of two-thirds being evaporated and the owner also says that two- thirds have been evaporated, only one-third has remained, then you can drink it.’”
